units.title: What Robots Are
units.blurb: Machines that sense, decide and act on their own, and the parts that do each job.

units.title: Build and Program
units.blurb: A first safe circuit, programs as steps and loops, and a cardboard arm you can make at the kitchen table.

topics.title: What Makes a Robot
topics.short: A robot senses the world, decides with a program, and acts, over and over.
topics.trouble: Children call any machine with motors a robot, even one a person steers every moment.

topics.title: Sensors and Motors
topics.short: Sensors are a robot's senses; motors, servos, lights and speakers are its muscles.
topics.trouble: Children mix up the two jobs and call a motor a sensor because it is part of the robot.

topics.title: A First Circuit
topics.short: Current flows only around a complete loop: battery, switch, resistor and LED.
topics.trouble: Children leave a gap in the loop, or put the LED in backward and think the parts are broken.

topics.title: Programs, Steps and Loops
topics.short: A program is a list of steps the robot follows in order; a loop repeats steps.
topics.trouble: Children count a turn as a move, or forget that a loop runs its steps more than once.

topics.title: A Cardboard Arm and a Bristlebot
topics.short: A lever arm moves its end farther than your hand, but with less force.
topics.trouble: Children expect a long arm to be both farther-reaching and stronger.
